verified_behavior: SQLite reopened from a real temporary file preserves chosen identity, notes, decisions and order; token hashes differ from bearer tokens.
Real authenticated namespace sockets receive only their active project stream; switching retrieves a chronological snapshot. Every authenticated workspace participant may join every project.
The same participant/attempt ID returns its existing entry without duplicate insert/broadcast; mismatched content is rejected.
Two independent browser contexts exchange literal notes/decisions and share a permalink, switch projects, retain drafts and reload identity/history.
Real disconnect misses peer entries; reconnection and a real server shutdown/restart recover them against the same SQLite file.
Controlled server handlers withhold acknowledgements with/without commit. Reload resolves an already saved attempt; explicit retry commits an unsaved attempt once. Newer typing survives both.
Explicit rejection preserves editable draft and removes uncertain retry state. Storage denial still permits current-session use with a persistent warning.
123 declared fixture entries paginate in chronological order; the actual downloaded JSON contains all 123, without credentials.
390-pixel workflow wraps a 500-character unbroken entry without horizontal document overflow; participant change retains earlier authorship.

review.material: Actual desktop/narrow screenshots and source/data flow
review.assessment: Distinct project selection, saved timeline, decision panel and export form one coherent workflow; current identity and delivery state remain visible. Source review protected newer typing, scoped drafts by participant, buffered join-time arrivals and made the 300-entry display limit explicit.

A test initially observed stale DOM during participant change; workspace now clears previous content and the test waits for the new identity.

preservation: P06/P03/P08/P10, P02 evaluation files/snapshot, archive and asset/transfer records unchanged against baseline. Legacy client/protocol/reading tests unchanged; server factory additionally returns app for room integration.
scope_limits: Trusted local workspace, default loopback; chosen names are not verified accounts and rooms are not access-controlled groups.
Node 24+ required for rooms/full suite; legacy entry retains Node 22 minimum and the evaluator lock graph. No added/upgraded package, hosted service or Sites deployment.
Single-server SQLite idempotency, not distributed exactly-once delivery; no automatic offline replay.
50-entry pages, 300 displayed timeline entries, latest 100 decisions; export includes every entry up to the 10,000/project cap.
Export is a consumable record, not restore/import. Full backup needs stopped SQLite data; active WAL main-file-only copying is insufficient.
Browser storage loss removes remembered identity/drafts; tokens lack revocation/expiry. Public identity/roles/TLS/retention, multiple writers and disaster recovery remain separate requirements.
No human usability, physical mobile/assistive technology, other-browser or commercial evidence. Test participants and project content are fictional fixtures.
Existing CI automatically runs the complete P11 suite; hosted outcomes must be read from Actions, not inferred from local results.
